title: GPU Hardware & Memory Budgets
description: Study compute, bandwidth and arithmetic intensity, training-state memory accounting, numerical formats and hardware support, and host offload and transfer costs. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Compute, bandwidth and arithmetic intensity
lessons.description: Classify matrix multiplication, data loading, and parameter synchronization by likely limiting resources.
lessons.conceptOverview: A GPU workload can be limited by arithmetic, memory movement, or communication. Arithmetic intensity relates operations to data moved. Larger theoretical compute does not help a workload stalled on memory or input preparation. Profiling identifies which resource actually limits the step.
lessons.whyItMatters: Optimize the measured resource bottleneck rather than peak compute alone.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A small operation repeatedly reading large arrays can be bandwidth-bound even on a powerful GPU.

keyTakeaways: Optimize the measured resource bottleneck rather than peak compute alone.

lessons.title: Training-state memory accounting
lessons.description: Build a component-by-component memory budget for an assumed optimizer and batch size.
lessons.conceptOverview: Training memory includes parameters, gradients, optimizer states, activations, and temporary buffers. Precision and optimizer implementation change bytes per parameter. Estimate these components separately and include allocator headroom; a weights-only estimate describes neither full training nor reliable deployment capacity.
lessons.whyItMatters: State assumptions for each memory component and reserve runtime headroom.

lessons.title: Numerical formats and hardware support
lessons.description: Document parameter, activation, gradient, optimizer, and reduction dtypes for one proposed configuration.
lessons.conceptOverview: FP16, BF16, FP32, and FP8 differ in exponent range and precision. Hardware and software kernels determine whether a format is supported efficiently. Low-precision recipes may keep selected state or reductions at higher precision. Storage dtype alone does not describe all arithmetic.
lessons.whyItMatters: Check the whole numerical recipe and hardware support.

lessons.title: Host offload and transfer costs
lessons.description: Estimate the transfer volume per step and identify whether transfers can overlap computation.
lessons.conceptOverview: Offloading state to CPU memory or storage can enable a larger model but adds transfer and scheduling costs. PCIe, host bandwidth, and storage latency can become bottlenecks. Compare end-to-end step time and effective utilization, not only whether the model fits.
lessons.whyItMatters: Offload exchanges accelerator memory pressure for data-movement overhead.
